items.title: Strategic Priority - Equitable Services and Opportunities
CSD-CHS-24-001, Increasing Space Opportunities for Community-Based Non-Profit Child Care Growth
notes:
Barb Cardow, Director of Children`s Services, provided an overview of the CSD-CHS-24-001, Increasing Space Opportunities for Community-Based Non-Profit Child Care Growth report. She identified that in the Region of Waterloo there have been 921 new child care spaces created between 2022 and 2023 and a service target of 1400 new spaces planned by 2026. The ratio target for child care spaces in the Region of Waterloo is 85% non-profit and 15% for-profit and the current ratio is 60% non-profit and 40% for-profit, accordingly, Staff have identified that non-profit growth needs to be a priority. She further identified that the amount of community based non-profit child care spaces on Regionally owned lands needs to be increased to meet the child care needs in the community as there is a shortage spaces available, specifically affordable spaces. 

Responding to the Committee, B. Cardow clarified that Staff will utilize the map provided to the Committee in 2023 that has the geographical priority areas for child care spaces based on the amount of children in the specified area and various risk indicators, such as socioeconomic status and shortage of licensed child care spaces. She further clarified that Staff are collaborating to identify the priority areas to provide options for families that are precariously housed.

In response to the Committee, B. Cardow explained that the waitlist for licensed child care has increased to 9,200 children which is a 115% increase following the introduction of the Canada-wide Early Learning and Child Care affordability plan. She further explained that non-profit child care has been prioritized because non-profit was determined to provide the highest quality care.

notes:
M. Harris provided a brief explanation of the proposed motion, and it was agreed to amend the motion to remove the language "prior to the distribution of funding". The amended motion was seconded and discussed by the Committee.

In responding to the Committee, Kelly-Anne Salerno, Assistant Director of Housing Operations & Administration, confirmed that the data collected from regionally funded organizations delivering supports would include data, such as referrals, unique households descriptions, and service restrictions.

The Committee proposed deferring the motion to provide A Better Tent City more time to review the proposed motion.

motions.item_title: CSD-CHS-24-001, Increasing Space Opportunities for Community-Based Non-Profit Child Care Growth
motions.text: That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following action with respect to implementing the Canada-wide Early Learning and Child Care (CWELCC) directed growth plan , which prioritizes non-profit growth as outlined in repor t CSD-CHS- 24-001 dated February 6, 2024 : Direct staff to explore, where feasible and appropriate, the development of community-based non-profit child care spaces in Regionally owned land/ buildings and surplus lands , Waterloo Region Housing redevelopments , and other emerging opportunities . Direct Children’s Services , Housing Services, and Economic Development staff to consult with area municipalities, school boards, universities and colleges , hospitals , other community partners and businesses to explore creating affordable spaces for community-based non-profit child care in under-utilized buildings and land s .
motions.text_html:
That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following action with respect to implementing the Canada-wide Early Learning and Child Care (CWELCC) directed growth plan, which prioritizes non-profit growth as outlined in report CSD-CHS-24-001 dated February 6, 2024:

  1. Direct staff to explore, where feasible and appropriate, the development of community-based non-profit child care spaces in Regionally owned land/buildings and surplus lands, Waterloo Region Housing redevelopments, and other emerging opportunities.

     

  2. Direct Children’s Services, Housing Services, and Economic Development staff to consult with area municipalities, school boards, universities and colleges, hospitals, other community partners and businesses to explore creating affordable spaces for community-based non-profit child care in under-utilized buildings and lands.

motions.item_title: Councillor M. Harris Notice of Motion
motions.text: Whereas, the Region of Waterloo is implementing its Interim Housing Plan while developing a Plan to End Chronic Homelessness, an unprecedented commitment using an all of community approach to ending chronic homelessness in Waterloo Region. Whereas, the 2024 Regional budget included an addition of $10.2 million to address, prevent and end chronic homelessness while the Plan to End Chronic Homelessness will be finalized and delivered in April of 2025, Whereas, an additional $236,390 grant was approved by Council for A Better Tent City, a volunteer-led organization that did not meet the criteria set out in the Region’s Fee-for-Service call for proposals to provide Community Outreach and Support Services, Whereas, agreement outcomes and accountabilities currently exist for similar outreach services funded by the Region of Waterloo, Therefore be it resolved that Regional staff be directed to collect outcomes, data and metrics from A Better Tent City that align with existing homelessness outreach agreements and providers and that such are agreed to with A Better Tent City.
motions.text_html:
Whereas, the Region of Waterloo is implementing its Interim Housing Plan while developing a Plan to End Chronic Homelessness, an unprecedented commitment using an all of community approach to ending chronic homelessness in Waterloo Region.

Whereas, the 2024 Regional budget included an addition of $10.2 million to address, prevent and end chronic homelessness while the Plan to End Chronic Homelessness will be finalized and delivered in April of 2025,

Whereas, an additional $236,390 grant was approved by Council for A Better Tent City, a volunteer-led organization that did not meet the criteria set out in the Region’s Fee-for-Service call for proposals to provide Community Outreach and Support Services,

Whereas, agreement outcomes and accountabilities currently exist for similar outreach services funded by the Region of Waterloo,

Therefore be it resolved that Regional staff be directed to collect outcomes, data and metrics from A Better Tent City that align with existing homelessness outreach agreements and providers and that such are agreed to with A Better Tent City.
